text.p: Italian debt markets tumbled at the finish, trading around 40 basis points down on the day in a fall led by the Bund market, brokers said.
Dealers could not pinpoint an exact reason for the late sell-off, saying it seemed the Bund fall had prompted players to take profits.

The Btp market was waiting for preliminary inflation data from seven sample Italian cities' due after 1530 GMT to confirm Tuesday's indications that May inflation is running at 1.5 percent year on year after 1.7 percent in April.

If the 1.5 percent rate is confirmed, brokers say many in the market are expecting the Bank of Italy to lop 50 to 75 basis points off the 6.75 percent discount rate either as early as this evening or by Friday. Others say the central bank could wait until after the first round of French elections this week but expectations for an easing are running very high.
"On a rate cut, it's really hard to say -- we reckon there's a 50 percent chance they'll cut tonight but it's more likely to be Friday," one broker in London said.
The June LIFFE contract was 39 basis points down at 130.50 while the February 2007 Btp was 36 bps off at 97.60.
